measurement: v2 G-TRIVIAL — and the test of whether the 64% localisation payoff is CAUSAL
the_rule_did_exactly_what_was_predicted_: 41.2% is the symptom-region rule's accuracy on these 80 tasks, predicted before the run from the task set alone. Localisation rose 10 points, from 31.2% to 41.2%.

AND_IT_BOUGHT_ONE_EPISODE_IN_EIGHTY.reading: THE 64% IS LARGELY SELECTION, NOT CAUSATION. The episodes the agent localises on its own are the EASY ones. Imposing correct localisation on the hard ones converts about one in eight. I flagged the 64% as an optimistic ceiling when I reported it; this measures how optimistic.

what_it_does_to_G's_expected_value: a head with PERFECT localisation would fix all 55 currently wrong first hypotheses. At the marginal 12.5% that is ~7 episodes: 20% -> ~28%, not the ~64% the naive ceiling implied. G is still worth running -- 8 points is a real effect and no prior this programme has tested has produced one -- but the target should be set from the marginal rate, not the conditional one.
and_the_0pct_is_unmoved: first hypothesis WRONG is 0% green in BOTH arms (55 and 47 episodes). The agent hypothesises once, so a wrong region is unrecoverable inside the budget. That half of the split is a harness property and it is stable.
bounds: 80 episodes, four slices, greedy. The +1 episode is inside noise; the claim that carries is the MARGINAL CONVERSION (12.5% vs 64%), which rests on 8 episodes and is itself thin.
G-trivial on v2 is handed task['bug_class'] (the true class) as on v1, so it is an oracle on the class as well as the region. It still bought one episode.
'Imposed' localisation is imposed on a DIFFERENT SUBSET than the agent chooses, so the comparison is between groups, not within. That is exactly why it measures selection.
